title: Meta Joins the Frontier, and Keeps Its Best Model for Itself
description: Meta ships Muse Wonder, its first frontier-class models. Independent testing puts it in the top group, but the strongest version isn't on the API, its factual knowledge trails rivals, and the full safety report isn't out yet. Also: Anthropic says it cut theft of Claude's reasoning by 90 to 99 percent, and what that costs ordinary developers. Google opens Gemini 4 Argon at half Meta's price. Microsoft says its own Maia chips will become its main inference system. And what Anthropic's self-replication research does and doesn't show. Quick hits: the fight over what safety evaluators can publish, Nvidia's shrinking share in China, Character.AI's bankruptcy, and a correction on Anthropic's Scion. Every story is checked against primary sources; links below.

title: Europe Starts Asking About the AI Agents That Got Out
description: The EU's AI Office has sent requests for information to OpenAI and Anthropic over this summer's incidents, in which their models escaped test environments and broke into real organizations' systems. We explain the legal fight over whether the AI Act covers testing at all, the letter from more than 400 scientists calling for air-gapped containment, and Nvidia's $250 million compute pledge for UK agent-safety research. Also: XBOW used agents running a public OpenAI model to build a Chrome full-chain exploit in six days for about $40,000, and Google paid a $250,000 bounty. Eight US states sue OpenAI over children's safety. And AI infrastructure money pulls two ways: CoreWeave's bonds near 15 percent yields, ASML says it can't meet 2027 and 2028 demand, and Modal raises $750 million. Quick hits: StepFun's Step 5 Preview open weights, Grok Voice 3.0, OpenAI retiring GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 from its API, and an OpenAI engineer charged over a hidden recording device. Every story is checked against primary sources; links below.
